payload.executive_summary: Candidate B01A specifies the most conservative Implementation Council design: Architecture option O1 (sequential, linear state machine) with a single end-to-end delivery milestone and a single final Freeze decision. The design prioritizes determinism, auditability, and strict governance (high HITL strictness, sandboxed tooling, network-deny baseline), enforcing: (1) canonical-only inputs (plan_package_final.json + structured handoff bundle), (2) immutable audit spine with checkpointed stage handoffs at every transition, (3) RFC 6901 JSON Pointer evidence across all canonical artifacts, (4) RFC 6902 JSON Patch-only repairs for JSON artifacts and diff-only patchsets for code, and (5) freeze gating only when all deterministic validators pass (build/test/lint/typecheck/security as applicable, integrity, workspace integrity, risk closure, reproducibility, and trace completeness).

architecture_choice.rationale: O1 is selected to maximize predictability and governance under an extremely risk-averse posture: a single linear, orchestrator-owned state machine yields an unambiguous audit trail, strict checkpoint boundaries, and simpler enforcement of separation of powers, tool permissions, and closure gates. This aligns with the branch’s “big-bang” acceptance strategy (one comprehensive freeze bundle) and high HITL strictness, reducing the chance of incremental drift, silent scope expansion, or audit spine breakage by constraining work into a single governed pipeline culminating in one final Freeze decision.
architecture_choice.high_level_dataflow: 1) Intake Gate validates plan_package_final.json (canonical-only), repo_context.json, and workspace_context.json; initializes immutable implementation_run_manifest and append-only implementation_event_log; emits stage_handoff for Intake→WorkPlanning. 2) Work Plan Compiler produces work_plan.json with ordered tasks and AT# trace mapping; emits stage_handoff. 3) Generate: Writer Pod produces diff-only patchset artifacts (no direct repo writes), constrained by repo_context forbidden/protected paths; emits stage_handoff. 4) PatchApply: orchestrator applies patchsets deterministically (base_commit pinned), enforcing operation caps and forbidden/protected paths; emits stage_handoff. 5) Validate: Validator Engine runs declared repo_context entrypoints (build/test/lint/typecheck/security/secrets) with deterministic retry policy; emits test_results/quality_reports plus gate status; emits stage_handoff. 6) Review: Reviewer Pod reads-only and emits findings-only review_findings.json with RFC6901 evidence pointers; emits stage_handoff. 7) Patch (if needed): Patcher Pod proposes bounded RFC6902 patches (JSON artifacts) and/or replacement diff-only patchsets; orchestrator selects smallest passing repair deterministically; loop bounded; emits stage_handoff. 8) Judge: Judge Pod produces trace_report.json and freeze/no-freeze recommendation with evidence-backed decisions; emits stage_handoff. 9) Freeze: Freeze Assembler validates presence of all CNS10 bundle artifacts + final integrity/reproducibility/workspace integrity + secrets scan; emits decision_record.json, release_bundle.json, and the Implementation Freeze Bundle.
key_design_decisions: Use a strictly sequential orchestrator-owned pipeline (no parallel lanes) to simplify auditability and deterministic replay.
Single comprehensive Freeze bundle is the only acceptance event (no partial-freeze semantics in this branch).
Deny-by-default tool permissions with sandboxed execution; network access denied by baseline policy; repo writes only via patch_apply of diff-only patchsets.
Enforce canonical-only planning semantics: accept plan_package_final.json (and structured handoff bundle) as sole authoritative input; deviations require ChangeRequest + escalation.
Mandate checkpointing via stage_handoff artifacts at every stage transition; absence blocks progress.
Single evidence standard across all canonical artifacts: RFC 6901 JSON Pointer objects into versioned JSON artifacts; no alternate citation formats.
Canonical JSON artifact modifications only via RFC 6902 JSON Patch; code changes only via diff-only patchset JSON artifacts.
Smallest-passing-repair selection is deterministic (fewest ops, fewest bytes, first-generated) when multiple passing repairs exist.

Freeze is permitted only when all closure gates pass (quality, security, integrity, workspace integrity, reproducibility, trace completeness, risk closure) and every decision/waiver is evidence-backed.

milestones.name: Big-bang sequential Implementation Council plan + governed Freeze Bundle contract (O1)

deliverables.text: Deterministic linear workflow specification (state machine) covering at minimum Intake → Generate → Validate → Review → Judge → Freeze, with explicit checkpoint boundaries and stage_handoff required at every transition (including any additional internal stages such as WorkPlanning/PatchApply/Patch).

Typed/versioned JSON schemas and contracts: repo_context.json, workspace_context.json, stage_handoff.json, ChangeRequest schema, work_plan.json, patchset schema (diff-only), and the full Implementation Freeze Bundle artifact set (CNS10/R7).

Governance and enforcement spec: tool permission matrix per stage/role, secrets detection/redaction/blocking rules, forbidden/protected path enforcement rules, operation caps, and deterministic retry/quarantine/escalation policy for flaky failures.

Validator and gate specification: deterministic code-owned validators for build/test/lint/typecheck (as applicable), security/secrets, artifact integrity, workspace integrity, reproducibility, risk closure (K#), and trace completeness (RFC6901 compliance + AT# mapping).
Traceability model and artifacts: evidence pointer standard usage rules, trace_report.json expectations, and test_results.json AT# mapping requirements sufficient to satisfy trace completeness gates.

Final Freeze bundle assembly definition: required bundle contents, directory layout (context_packs/, stage_handoffs/), bundle manifest expectations, and decision_record.json evidence-backed decision/waiver rules.

exit_criteria: All MUST requirements R1–R23 are explicitly addressed by the architecture/workflow/contracts and are verifiable by acceptance tests AT1–AT23.

Architecture option O1 is fully specified with clear responsibilities across orchestrator, workspace gateway, writer/reviewer/patcher/judge pods, validator engine, and freeze assembler, preserving separation of powers and writer/reviewer/judge separation.

Every stage transition in the defined pipeline requires emission of a schema-valid stage_handoff artifact containing objectives, completed work references, blockers, next actions, and RFC6901 evidence pointers into canonical artifacts (work_plan, patchsets, validation outputs).

Freeze bundle minimum contents are enumerated exactly as required (implementation_run_manifest.json, implementation_event_log.jsonl, work_plan.json, patchsets, repo_snapshot.json, test_results.json, quality_reports.json, trace_report.json, review_findings.json, release_bundle.json, decision_record.json, workspace_index.json, context_packs/, stage_handoffs/).

Deterministic enforcement rules are defined for: canonical-only planning semantics, RFC6901-only evidence pointers, RFC6902-only canonical JSON repairs, diff-only patchsets for code changes, forbidden/protected path blocking, deterministic smallest-passing-repair selection, and deterministic retry/quarantine/escalation logging.
HITL triggers and approval roles are defined for critical policy events (secrets, protected path touches, critical security findings, retry budget exhaustion, gate waivers, ChangeRequests).

decision_log.question: Which architecture option is selected for candidate B01A?
decision_log.choice: Select O1 (sequential staged pipeline with explicit role pods and an orchestrator-owned linear state machine).
decision_log.rationale: The branch is explicitly the most conservative and risk-averse; O1 minimizes orchestration complexity and makes auditability/checkpointing/tool-policy enforcement simplest to specify and validate deterministically, aligning with separation of powers and durable audit spine constraints.
what_would_change_this_decision: If wall-clock time or token/time budgets regularly fail under serialized execution (see Q13), consider O3 for checkpoint-driven partial freezes or O2 for deterministic parallel lanes.
If integration conflicts become a primary risk driver requiring specialized integration governance, consider O2.
If external interface simplicity is prioritized over modular stage enforcement (despite governance risk), consider O4.

evidence_pointers.note: O1 sequential staged pipeline option definition
evidence_pointers.quote: O1: Sequential staged pipeline with explicit council role pods... linear state machine.

evidence_pointers.note: Branch selection includes selected_arch_option_id=O1 and risk-averse rationale
evidence_pointers.quote: selected_arch_option_id: O1; most conservative and risk-averse approach.

decision_log.question: What acceptance strategy is used for this candidate (incremental vs single final freeze)?
decision_log.choice: Single comprehensive Freeze acceptance (“big-bang”): all requirements and acceptance tests must pass in one final freeze bundle; no partial-freeze acceptance events.
decision_log.rationale: This branch’s governance posture prioritizes holistic review and minimizing incremental drift; a single freeze gate concentrates approval into one evidence-backed decision point and reduces the risk of partially accepted states being misinterpreted as complete.
alternatives_considered: Incremental freezes after subsets of tasks (would resemble O3 partial-freeze semantics)
Parallel lane completion with integration acceptance (O2)
what_would_change_this_decision: If long-horizon work frequently exceeds deterministic budgets (Q13) and progress must be preserved, adopt O3-style partial freeze with explicit resume descriptors.
If repository decomposition supports safe parallelism without increasing merge-risk beyond thresholds (K12), consider O2 with deterministic integration acceptance.

evidence_pointers.note: Branch acceptance strategy
evidence_pointers.quote: Acceptance is based on a single, comprehensive freeze bundle passing all gates at the end.

evidence_pointers.note: Freeze gating requirement (all closure gates must pass)
evidence_pointers.quote: Freeze SHALL be permitted only when all deterministic, code-owned closure gates pass.

decision_log.question: How is auditability and resumability enforced across stages?
decision_log.choice: Require immutable run_manifest + append-only event_log + checkpoint at every stage boundary, including a required stage_handoff artifact at every transition.
decision_log.rationale: This is the core mechanism to ensure deterministic replay/resume without relying on chat logs or transient memory, and to preserve a durable audit spine with explicit stage boundary artifacts.
alternatives_considered: Checkpoint only at major milestones (insufficient for R5/R8)
Implicit handoff via event log only (insufficient operational resumability per R6)
what_would_change_this_decision: If storage/checkpoint overhead becomes prohibitive, optimize artifact payload sizes and introduce deterministic compaction for non-canonical data (K22) without removing stage handoff requirements.
If resumption demands finer granularity than stage transitions, adopt task-level checkpoints (O3).

evidence_pointers.note: Stage handoff required at every checkpoint boundary
evidence_pointers.quote: At every checkpoint boundary... SHALL emit a stage_handoff JSON artifact.

evidence_pointers.note: Audit spine immutability and checkpointing
evidence_pointers.quote: run_manifest immutable; event_log append-only; checkpoint canonical artifacts at every stage boundary.

decision_log.question: What is the sole evidence/traceability standard used in canonical artifacts?
decision_log.choice: RFC 6901 JSON Pointer evidence pointer objects referencing versioned JSON artifacts; reject any alternative citation formats.
decision_log.rationale: A single, validator-checkable citation mechanism is required to keep traceability machine-verifiable and prevent informal or non-resolvable evidence references that break downstream consumption.
alternatives_considered: Allow file-path/code-pointer citations in addition to JSON Pointers (forbidden by constraints)
Allow prose citations within artifacts (breaks validation and determinism)
what_would_change_this_decision: If the artifact store cannot support stable artifact_ref addressing and pointer resolution (A2/Q3), the storage/evidence contract must be clarified upstream before proceeding.
If repo state cannot be represented as JSON artifacts for citation (R11), additional state-capture schemas must be specified (without changing the evidence standard).

evidence_pointers.note: Single evidence pointer standard requirement
evidence_pointers.quote: All evidence pointers... SHALL use a single standard: RFC 6901 JSON Pointer objects...

evidence_pointers.note: Citeable state must be represented as versioned JSON artifacts
evidence_pointers.quote: Repository, code, and workspace state... SHALL be represented as versioned JSON artifacts...

evidence_pointers.note: Risk K3: evidence standard not used consistently
evidence_pointers.quote: Evidence pointer standard not used consistently... causes unverifiable traceability.

decision_log.question: What mutation/repair mechanisms are allowed for canonical JSON artifacts and for code changes?
decision_log.choice: Canonical JSON artifacts may only be modified via RFC 6902 JSON Patch arrays; all code changes may only be emitted/applied via diff-only patchset JSON artifacts with deterministic apply order.
decision_log.rationale: Constraining mutation mechanisms makes repairs auditable, bounded, and validator-enforceable, preventing silent/implicit edits and supporting deterministic replay.
alternatives_considered: Direct replacement of canonical artifacts (forbidden by R12)
Direct repo writes by agents or tools (forbidden by R13/R14/tool policy)
what_would_change_this_decision: If patch application requires a different diff representation (Q7), update the patchset schema while preserving diff-only and deterministic-apply constraints.
If certain canonical artifacts need controlled regeneration, it must still be expressed as JSON Patch deltas applied by orchestrator-controlled repair logic.

evidence_pointers.note: JSON Patch-only repairs for canonical JSON
evidence_pointers.quote: Repairs to canonical JSON artifacts SHALL be expressed exclusively as RFC 6902 JSON Patch arrays.

evidence_pointers.note: Diff-only patchsets for code changes
evidence_pointers.quote: All code changes... SHALL be emitted exclusively as diff-only patchset JSON artifacts...

evidence_pointers.note: Forbidden/protected-path rules and operation caps during patch apply
evidence_pointers.quote: No patchset may write to paths declared forbidden/protected in repo_context.json...

evidence_pointers.note: Smallest passing repair selection tie-breakers
evidence_pointers.quote: Select the smallest passing repair... fewest operations, fewest bytes changed, first-generated.

decision_log.question: What governance posture is applied to tool permissions and environment access?
decision_log.choice: Sandboxed, deny-by-default tool permission matrix with network denied by baseline; repo writes only via orchestrator-controlled patch_apply; all tool policy violations are blocked and recorded in the event log; high HITL strictness for policy expansions and protected-path/security events.
decision_log.rationale: This posture reduces attack surface (secrets/supply chain) and prevents policy bypass or repo protection violations, aligning with the branch’s extreme risk aversion and critical risks (K5/K7/K15/K19).
alternatives_considered: Allow network access during Generate/Validate by default (increases K15)
Permit broad repo writes by tools/agents (increases K5/K19)
what_would_change_this_decision: If target repos require dependency fetching and no offline mirror exists (Q11), introduce an explicitly allowlisted network stage with strict lockfile and domain allowlists while preserving deterministic logging and gating.
If certain validations require controlled network calls (e.g., license checks), treat them as explicit exceptions requiring HITL approval and captured evidence.

evidence_pointers.note: Repo protection bypass risk and mitigation
evidence_pointers.quote: Repository protection bypass... enforce forbidden/protected-path controls at patch-apply time and tool-sandbox policy.

evidence_pointers.note: Secrets leakage risk and mitigation
evidence_pointers.quote: Mandatory secrets scanning at each checkpoint and before freeze...

evidence_pointers.note: Supply-chain/network risk and mitigation
evidence_pointers.quote: Default network deny; allow network only in designated stages with allowlisted domains...

evidence_pointers.note: Tool permission misconfiguration risk and mitigation
evidence_pointers.quote: Machine-enforced tool permission matrix per stage with deny-by-default...

evidence_pointers.note: Conservative stage tool policies (network deny baseline)
evidence_pointers.quote: network: deny baseline; repo_write only via patch_apply in PatchApply stage.

decision_log.question: How is separation of powers enforced among writers, reviewers, and judges?
decision_log.choice: Enforce writer/reviewer/judge separation via orchestrator routing and output-type allowlists: reviewers are findings-only (no patches/writing), judges are decision/trace only; multi-vendor routing required across these roles.
decision_log.rationale: Role separation and multi-vendor diversity reduce conflicts of interest and governance failure modes (K10), ensuring independent critique and evidence-backed acceptance decisions.
alternatives_considered: Allow a single agent to write + review + judge (violates R22/CNS12)
Allow reviewers to propose patches directly (violates findings-only constraint)
what_would_change_this_decision: If the available model portfolio cannot satisfy multi-vendor separation (A5/Q5), reroute to policy owners to define an acceptable deterministic separation strategy (e.g., model-family separation or HITL reviewer substitution).

If certain stages require combined roles due to staffing constraints, require explicit HITL exception with recorded rationale and evidence, and adjust validators accordingly (but this conflicts with MUST constraints).

evidence_pointers.note: Role separation and reviewers findings-only requirement
evidence_pointers.quote: Writers produce outputs; reviewers produce findings-only; judges produce accept/reject decisions; multi-vendor routing enforced.

evidence_pointers.note: Role separation failure risk and mitigation
evidence_pointers.quote: Orchestrator-enforced output-type allowlists by role... multi-vendor routing constraints.

decision_log.question: How are scope/semantics protected against silent expansion relative to the frozen upstream plan?
decision_log.choice: Treat plan_package_final.json as the sole authority for semantics; forbid semantic changes to R#/AT#/O#/K#; require ChangeRequest + decision record + policy escalation (HITL and/or reroute upstream) before any semantic deviation is applied.
decision_log.rationale: This is the primary guardrail against silent scope expansion (K1) and preserves upstream governance, ensuring downstream work remains an implementation of the frozen plan rather than a re-planning exercise.
alternatives_considered: Allow “minor” semantic edits without ChangeRequest (not allowed)
Let implementers reinterpret acceptance criteria to make validation easier (not allowed)
what_would_change_this_decision: If the intake validator finds the upstream plan ambiguous/incomplete (K20), the correct path is reroute upstream rather than relaxing no-scope-expansion constraints.
If organizational policy changes to permit certain classes of downstream clarifications, they must still be captured as ChangeRequests with explicit approvals and traceability.

evidence_pointers.note: No semantic change without ChangeRequest + escalation
evidence_pointers.quote: SHALL NOT modify semantics... deviations require ChangeRequest + decision record + escalation before applied.

evidence_pointers.note: Risk K1: silent plan-semantics drift
evidence_pointers.quote: Silent plan-semantics drift / scope expansion... requires deterministic semantic-drift/trace gates.

evidence_pointers.note: Risk K20: upstream plan ambiguity
evidence_pointers.quote: If validation fails, orchestrator immediately reroutes upstream... rather than allowing assumption-based implementation.

supplemental_evaluations.title: Risk-posture alignment (B01A vs K1/K2/K5/K7/K10)
supplemental_evaluations.notes: B01A’s linear O1 pipeline plus high HITL strictness and deny-by-default tool policy is strongly aligned with the highest-severity governance risks: preventing silent scope expansion (K1) via ChangeRequest gating; protecting the audit spine (K2) via immutable manifest + append-only event log and mandatory checkpoints; blocking repo protection bypass (K5) via forbidden/protected path enforcement and patch_apply-only repo writes; preventing secrets persistence (K7) via checkpoint-time scans and blocking; and enforcing independence (K10) via role separation and multi-vendor routing. The primary residual concern is operational scalability under a single serialized lane (risk of budget exhaustion and long-horizon stalls), which is highlighted in synthesis warnings.

evidence.quote: Repository protection bypass: patchsets or tools modify forbidden/protected paths...
Secrets leakage into canonical artifacts or workspace...
Role separation failure... multi-vendor diversity not enforced...

synthesis_warnings.summary: Big-bang sequential execution (O1 + single final Freeze) may be incompatible with long-horizon repos and deterministic token/time budgets; Q13 remains blocking for whether partial freezes/checkpoint micro-cycles are required.
